question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

How long / have you / been learn / English now?
solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. been learn .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **present perfect continuous tense**, which is used to talk about actions that started in the past and are still ongoing or were recently completed.
 
• The correct structure for the present perfect continuous tense is: **have/has + been + base verb + ing**.
 
• In the given sentence, "been learn" is incorrect because the verb "learn" should be in the present participle form (learning) to match the structure.

Correct sentence: *How long have you been learning English now?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect Continuous Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + have/has + been + base verb + ing.
 
• **Example:** They have been working on the project since morning.
 
• **Usage: **Describes actions that started in the past and are still happening or have just been completed.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**

 
 
• Using the base verb instead of the present participle (e.g., "been learn" instead of "been learning").
 
• Omitting "been" in the structure (e.g., "have learning" instead of "have been learning").
